holidays.name: National Fettuccine Alfredo Day
holidays.description: A day to twirl your fork through a bowl of buttery, cheesy, creamy noodles. Carb-loading is the whole point, and nobody will judge a second helping.
holidays.origin: The dish dates to 1908 in Rome. Restaurateur Alfredo di Lelio is said to have invented it to help his pregnant wife get her appetite back. It was named after him. The creator of the holiday itself is unknown.
holidays.funFact: Fettuccine noodles first appeared in Florence during the Renaissance. It took centuries before someone tossed them with butter and cheese and made the famous dish.

holidays.name: National Periodic Table Day
holidays.description: A day for chemistry fans to celebrate the colorful chart that organizes every known element. Wear your favorite element on a T-shirt, try a safe experiment, or learn what the weird symbols stand for.
holidays.origin: Chemistry teacher and inventor David T. Steineker of Kentucky founded it in 2016. The date honors the early work on organizing the elements that led up to Mendeleev's 1869 table.
holidays.funFact: An early attempt at a periodic table was John Newlands' 'Law of Octaves'. It sorted 56 elements into groups, and it was eventually disproven. It still helped pave the way for Mendeleev's table, which chemists use today.

holidays.name: Wave All Your Fingers at Your Neighbor Day
holidays.description: A day for giving the people next door a big, silly wiggle-fingered wave. It's a tiny, free way to spread goofy goodwill on the block.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance of unclear origin, passed along by holiday calendars. It's a community-style celebration with no known founder.
holidays.funFact: The holiday asks for every finger, not just a polite palm wave. A halfhearted two-finger salute doesn't count.
